intro: Chopin sets a slow F-major song against a Presto in A minor, then lets the second key take possession of the ending. Frank Lévy’s recording makes the difference in scale between the quiet melody and its interruptions a useful guide to the form.
question: How does the opening song change when A minor replaces F major?

cues.title: Two keys, two speeds
cues.text: The opening sings in F major at an Andantino pace. The contrasting music is a Presto in A minor: Chopin changes speed, texture and tonal centre together. Keep the opening’s unhurried phrase in mind.

cues.title: A melody in chords
cues.text: Through the opening, listen to the upper line and the notes moving beneath it. Chordal writing can suggest several singers on one instrument; the melody need not carry every change in the harmony.
cues.evidence: General listening invitation for the opening chordal texture; no individual note or entrance is located.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: A dedication to Schumann
cues.text: Chopin dedicated this Ballade to Robert Schumann. In October 1840 Schumann recorded his pleasure at the dedication and reviewed the work in the Neue Zeitschrift für Musik.
cues.evidence: Tomaszewski quotes Schumann’s diary and review: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

cues.title: Quiet before contrast
cues.text: The opening span draws back before the first fast interruption. Listen to how much space the soft chordal texture leaves: the contrast will involve the density of attacks as well as volume.
cues.evidence: cache/analysis/chopin-ballade-2.txt: level falls to about −27 to −28 dB at 1:50–2:00; the 2:04 novelty peak precedes much louder, denser activity.

cues.title: The first interruption
cues.text: In this passage the Presto replaces the quiet song with rapid figuration and forceful accents. A minor, rather than F major’s relative D minor, is the competing tonal centre.
cues.evidence: Strongest report boundary at 2:04; level rises from −27.9 dB at 2:00 to −6.2 dB at 2:05. Tomaszewski identifies the A-minor Presto: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: Motion beneath the accents
cues.text: During the fast music, separate the stream of small notes from the larger accents. Following both levels makes the return to a slower phrase more than a simple change of loudness.
cues.evidence: Listening invitation for the documented Presto texture; the report shows sustained high activity from 2:05 before a decline after 2:55.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: The song returns
cues.text: The slower material recovers its place after the first Presto. Its return does not guarantee a stable ending: Chopin will move the familiar melody through new harmonic surroundings.
cues.evidence: Report boundary 3:14 and low-density F-major-coloured windows at 3:15–3:25 support the approximate return; the formal reading comes from https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A different remembered ending
cues.text: Schumann remembered Chopin playing an earlier version in Leipzig that ended in F major. The published Ballade ends in A minor. His testimony suggests an earlier conception; no recording of Chopin survives to settle the difference.
cues.evidence: Schumann’s account and its evidential limits are discussed by Tomaszewski: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

cues.title: A swell inside quiet music
cues.text: This slower region contains a strong rise and retreat of its own. Listen for the melody gathering weight without mistaking every local increase in force for the return of the Presto.
cues.evidence: Report: level rises from −23.1 dB at 4:15 to −6.6 at 4:25, then falls to −24.7 at 4:45; this anchors a contour, not a new tempo.

cues.title: Poetry without a plot
cues.text: Schumann reported Chopin mentioning Mickiewicz’s poems as a stimulus for his ballades. No particular poem has been securely matched to this score. The alternation of song and interruption can be followed without assigning characters to the themes.
cues.evidence: Tomaszewski distinguishes Schumann’s reported conversation from speculative identifications of individual poems: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

cues.title: The Presto takes over
cues.text: The rapid material returns and sustains its pressure for longer. Compare this broad fast span with the first interruption: the balance of the piece has shifted away from the opening’s leisurely song.
cues.evidence: Report: a sustained rise begins around 5:20, with loud, dense A-centred windows at 5:35–6:00; boundary estimated at 5:34, not bar-aligned. Formal succession: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: The bass still matters
cues.text: Throughout the fast passages, listen below the right-hand figuration. Changes in the bass redirect the harmony even when the surface seems to repeat the same kind of motion.
cues.evidence: General invitation, not a claim about a particular bass pitch at 6:10.
cues.how: A general description of this stretch of music.

cues.title: An agitated conclusion
cues.text: The concluding fast stretch presses the accumulated conflict towards a cadence. Listen for how the continuous figuration makes the eventual return of a few quiet melodic notes sound exposed.
cues.evidence: Agitato coda is placed approximately at 6:34: report density rises to 5.0–5.6 onsets/s around 6:35–6:55 after a dip at 6:30. The event is passage-level, not a counted bar.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: A final sustained crest
cues.text: The later fast music reaches another broad crest before it gives way. Hold the quiet opening in memory while the piano occupies a much larger dynamic range.
cues.evidence: Report lists 7:20 and 7:25 among the loudest five-second windows, followed by a steep fall at 7:35–7:40.

cues.title: A changed last word
cues.text: The closing recollection of the song belongs to A minor, not the opening F major. The work ends by changing the meaning of familiar material rather than restoring the first tonal home.
cues.evidence: Quiet closing region follows the 7:36 boundary; the A-minor ending is documented by https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96. The report’s late A-major estimates are not used to identify the written chord.
cues.how: Placed from the score’s proportions; the timing is approximate.

transitions.title: Song gives way to rapid figuration
transitions.how: The F-major song does not modulate gradually into a neighbouring lyrical theme. Chopin opposes it with an A-minor Presto: the broad chordal phrase gives way to fast broken figures and stronger accents. The same piano now supplies both a more active surface and a more forceful bass.
transitions.evidence: Strong boundary at 2:04 and level/density jump at 2:05 anchor the join approximately; tonal and textural design: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

transitions.title: The fast texture releases the song
transitions.how: The first Presto loses momentum and the Andantino texture returns. The upper melody can again be heard against relatively separated supporting chords. Recovering the song’s rhythm and F-major surroundings provides recognition, but its continuation will move beyond a literal repetition.
transitions.evidence: Report boundary 3:14; 3:15–3:25 restores low density and F-major colour. Approximate form reading: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

transitions.title: The opposition becomes a sustained argument
transitions.how: The song’s changing harmonic continuation yields to the rapid A-minor material again. Returning figuration joins the earlier interruption to a longer fast conclusion. Register, accents and the active bass enlarge the contrast without requiring a third principal theme.
transitions.evidence: Rise around 5:20–5:40 anchors the broader junction; 5:34 is an estimate of the Presto return, not an automatic theme detection. https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

transitions.title: Rapid motion becomes the closing argument
transitions.how: The fast episode feeds an Agitato coda rather than stopping for a separate tune. The hands maintain their rapid movement while sequences and accents compress the approach to the final cadence. A minor remains the destination of this extension, replacing the F-major home promised at the opening.
transitions.evidence: Approximate coda placement follows a 6:30 dip and denser 6:35–6:55 windows; the score’s broad concluding function is not fixed to a bar.

transitions.title: The song survives in the other key
transitions.how: The energetic coda subsides and a fragment of the opening song is recalled quietly. Its texture and melodic identity look backwards, but A minor changes its tonal meaning. The closing reminiscence therefore resolves the conflict by accepting the second key, not by returning to F major.
transitions.evidence: Boundary 7:36; level falls by about 20 dB between 7:30 and 7:40. Closing key and recollection: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/96

facts: Wojciech Żywny; Józef Elsner at Warsaw’s Main School of Music, 1826–29
Warsaw until 1830; Paris from 1831; summers at George Sand’s house in Nohant
Teaching, publication and selected performances, more often in salons than large public halls
Almost entirely centred on the piano: études, mazurkas, polonaises, nocturnes, preludes, ballades, scherzos, sonatas and concertos
composer.background:
Chopin was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810, to a French-born father, Nicolas, and a Polish mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska. The family soon moved to Warsaw, where Nicolas taught French. The name Fryderyk belongs to his Polish life; Frédéric became usual in France. His family observed his birthday on 1 March, although the baptismal record gives 22 February. Piano lessons with Wojciech Żywny introduced Bach and Mozart alongside the fashionable repertory of the day. As a child he composed polonaises and played in aristocratic houses, but his later musical education extended beyond the cultivation of a prodigy.

Józef Elsner taught him harmony and composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music from 1826 to 1829. Chopin heard Italian opera, encountered Polish vernacular music during visits outside the capital and learned the working forms of the virtuoso concerto. The F minor Concerto was composed before the E minor, despite their eventual numbering as Nos. 2 and 1. Both preserve an extended orchestral opening, but once the piano enters, its vocal line and ornament determine the movement’s scale. The slow movements belong as much to operatic singing as to the display repertory of a concert pianist.
composer.born: 1 March 1810, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: He made the piano sing through ornament, contrapuntal voice-leading and the unstable accents of Polish dance.
